<!-- Generated by web/docs/tools/generate-sdk-reference.py. Do not edit. -->

This reference lists the public Rust SDK interfaces, including signatures, resource helpers, and model types, so you can look up how to call the SDK and interpret its results.
Start with [Getting started with the SDK](/sdk/); see [Errors and recovery](/sdk/errors/) for connection lifetime, deadlines, and retries.

## capsem_sdk::Hypervisor

```rust
pub struct Hypervisor { /* private fields */ }

// A gateway connection. Clones and VM handles share the HTTP connection pool.

pub fn new(url: &str, token: &str) -> Result<Self>

pub fn with_timeout(self, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Self>

// Set this handle’s HTTP deadline, including response body reads.

pub async fn info(&self) -> Result<HypervisorInfo>

pub async fn restart(&self) -> Result<RestartResponse>

// Restart an idle managed service. Reconnect with a fresh gateway token.

pub async fn list(&self) -> Result<ListResponse>

pub fn vm(&self, selector: VmSelector) -> Result<VM>

pub fn networks(&self) -> Networks<'_>

pub fn images(&self) -> Images<'_>

pub fn credentials(&self) -> Credentials<'_>

pub fn connections(&self) -> Connections<'_>

pub fn mcp(&self) -> Mcp<'_>

// The MCP servers every VM runs, from settings and corp config.

pub fn debug(&self) -> Debug<'_>

pub async fn create(&self, options: CreateOptions) -> Result<VM>

pub async fn log(
    &self,
    source: HostLogSource,
    options: LogOptions,
) -> Result<HostLogsResponse>

pub async fn run(
    &self,
    command: &str,
    options: RunOptions,
) -> Result<ExecResponse>

pub async fn purge(&self, all: bool) -> Result<PurgeResponse>

pub async fn update(&self) -> Result<UpdateActionResponse>

pub async fn with_managed<T, F, Fut>(
    &self,
    options: CreateOptions,
    work: F,
) -> Result<T>where
    T: Send + 'static,
    F: FnOnce(VM, CancellationToken) -> Fut + Send + 'static,
    Fut: Future<Output = Result<T>> + Send + 'static,

// Create an unnamed ephemeral VM, renew ownership, and await cleanup after the callback. Dropping this future signals cancellation; its owned task continues cleanup on the runtime.
```

## capsem_sdk::VM

```rust
pub struct VM { /* private fields */ }

// A VM handle. Clones share canonical identity and the HTTP connection pool.

pub async fn log(&self, options: LogOptions) -> Result<LogsResponse>

pub async fn history(&self, options: HistoryOptions) -> Result<HistoryResponse>

pub async fn timeline(
    &self,
    options: TimelineOptions,
) -> Result<TimelineResponse>

pub fn container(&self) -> Container<'_>

pub fn ports(&self) -> Ports<'_>

pub fn files(&self) -> Files<'_>

pub fn networks(&self) -> VmNetworks<'_>

pub fn credential_grants(&self) -> CredentialGrants<'_>

pub fn new(url: &str, token: &str, selector: VmSelector) -> Result<Self>

pub fn with_timeout(self, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Self>

pub fn id(&self) -> Option<&str>

// Known immediately for ID selection, or after the first name lookup.

pub fn name(&self) -> Option<&str>

pub async fn info(&self) -> Result<SandboxInfo>

pub async fn exec(
    &self,
    command: &str,
    timeout_secs: Option<u64>,
) -> Result<ExecResponse>

pub async fn start(&self) -> Result<ProvisionResponse>

pub async fn stop(&self) -> Result<StopResponse>

pub async fn pause(&self) -> Result<VmActionResponse>

pub async fn resume(&self) -> Result<ProvisionResponse>

pub async fn delete(&self) -> Result<VmActionResponse>

pub async fn fork(
    &self,
    name: &str,
    description: Option<String>,
) -> Result<Self>

pub async fn persist(&self, name: &str) -> Result<PersistResponse>

pub fn stats(&self) -> Stats<'_>
```

## capsem_sdk::ManagedSession

```rust
pub struct ManagedSession { /* private fields */ }

// Recovery authority returned with a failed close. Debug never includes its capability.

pub fn ownership(&self) -> Option<&ManagedSessionOwnership>

// Last validated metadata from this ownership generation.

pub async fn close(&mut self, outcome: ManagedSessionOutcome) -> Result<()>

// Await original-generation cleanup. Failed requests retain authority for explicit retry.
```

## capsem_sdk::Error

```rust
pub enum Error {
    VmLookup {
        name: String,
        matches: usize,
    },
    InvalidInput(&'static str),
    InvalidResponse(&'static str),
    Cancelled,
    Managed(&'static str),
    ManagedCleanup {
        source: Box<Error>,
        session: Box<ManagedSession>,
    },
    Transport(Error),
    Http {
        status: u16,
        body: Vec<u8>,
    },
    Json(Error),
    Stream(String),
}

// Errors retain HTTP status and response bytes without exposing credentials.

pub fn credential_code(&self) -> Option<CredentialErrorCode>

// The broker’s sanitized machine-readable refusal, when present. Unknown future codes or malformed/non-JSON responses retain their HTTP error.
```

## capsem_sdk::CancellationToken

```rust
pub struct CancellationToken { /* private fields */ }

// A token which can be used to signal a cancellation request to one or more tasks. Tasks can call CancellationToken::cancelled() in order to obtain a Future which will be resolved when cancellation is requested. Cancellation can be requested through the CancellationToken::cancel method. §Examples use tokio::select; use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken; #[tokio::main] async fn main() { let token = CancellationToken::new(); let cloned_token = token.clone(); let join_handle = tokio::spawn(async move { // Wait for either cancellation or a very long time select! { _ = cloned_token.cancelled() => { // The token was cancelled 5 } _ = tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(9999)) => { 99 } } }); tokio::spawn(async move { tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10)).await; token.cancel(); }); assert_eq!(5, join_handle.await.unwrap()); }

pub fn new() -> CancellationToken

// Creates a new CancellationToken in the non-cancelled state.

pub fn child_token(&self) -> CancellationToken

// Creates a CancellationToken which will get cancelled whenever the current token gets cancelled. Unlike a cloned CancellationToken, cancelling a child token does not cancel the parent token. If the current token is already cancelled, the child token will get returned in cancelled state. §Examples use tokio::select; use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken; #[tokio::main] async fn main() { let token = CancellationToken::new(); let child_token = token.child_token(); let join_handle = tokio::spawn(async move { // Wait for either cancellation or a very long time select! { _ = child_token.cancelled() => { // The token was cancelled 5 } _ = tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(9999)) => { 99 } } }); tokio::spawn(async move { tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10)).await; token.cancel(); }); assert_eq!(5, join_handle.await.unwrap()); }

pub fn cancel(&self)

// Cancel the CancellationToken and all child tokens which had been derived from it. This will wake up all tasks which are waiting for cancellation. Be aware that cancellation is not an atomic operation. It is possible for another thread running in parallel with a call to cancel to first receive true from is_cancelled on one child node, and then receive false from is_cancelled on another child node. However, once the call to cancel returns, all child nodes have been fully cancelled.

pub fn is_cancelled(&self) -> bool

// Returns true if the CancellationToken is cancelled.

pub fn cancelled(&self) -> WaitForCancellationFuture<'_>

// Returns a Future that gets fulfilled when cancellation is requested. Equivalent to: ⓘasync fn cancelled(&self); The future will complete immediately if the token is already cancelled when this method is called. §Cancellation safety This method is cancel safe.

pub fn cancelled_owned(self) -> WaitForCancellationFutureOwned

// Returns a Future that gets fulfilled when cancellation is requested. Equivalent to: ⓘasync fn cancelled_owned(self); The future will complete immediately if the token is already cancelled when this method is called. The function takes self by value and returns a future that owns the token. §Cancellation safety This method is cancel safe.

pub fn drop_guard(self) -> DropGuard

// Creates a [DropGuard] for this token. Returned guard will cancel this token (and all its children) on drop unless disarmed.

pub fn drop_guard_ref(&self) -> DropGuardRef<'_>

// Creates a [DropGuardRef] for this token. Returned guard will cancel this token (and all its children) on drop unless disarmed.

pub async fn run_until_cancelled<F>(
    &self,
    fut: F,
) -> Option<<F as Future>::Output>where
    F: Future,

// Runs a future to completion and returns its result wrapped inside of an Option unless the CancellationToken is cancelled. In that case the function returns None and the future gets dropped. §Fairness Calling this on an already-cancelled token directly returns None. For all subsequent polls, in case of concurrent completion and cancellation, this is biased towards the future completion. §Cancellation safety This method is only cancel safe if fut is cancel safe.

pub async fn run_until_cancelled_owned<F>(
    self,
    fut: F,
) -> Option<<F as Future>::Output>where
    F: Future,

// Runs a future to completion and returns its result wrapped inside of an Option unless the CancellationToken is cancelled. In that case the function returns None and the future gets dropped. The function takes self by value and returns a future that owns the token. §Fairness Calling this on an already-cancelled token directly returns None. For all subsequent polls, in case of concurrent completion and cancellation, this is biased towards the future completion. §Cancellation safety This method is only cancel safe if fut is cancel safe.
```

```rust
// The session’s OCI workload, as the image’s own user, under the workload’s namespaces, seccomp filter, capabilities and cgroup.

// The VM, as VM root: Capsem’s diagnostics and the image runtime.
```

```rust
pub struct VmSummary {Show 18 fields
    pub id: String,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub status: VmLifecycleState,
    pub persistent: bool,
    pub uptime_secs: Option<u64>,

    pub can_resume: bool,
    pub resume_blocked_reason: Option<String>,
    pub last_error: Option<String>,
    pub available_actions: Vec<VmAction>,
}

// Why a crashed VM died: the process.log tail the service captured. The service splits the two on purpose – a defunct session carries its reason here and leaves resume_blocked_reason empty – so a consumer that reads only the latter has nothing to show for the one state where the user most needs a reason.
```

## capsem_api::Value

```rust
pub type Value = Value;

// Extensible MCP arguments and results retain their native JSON shape.

pub enum Value {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Number(Number),
    String(String),
    Array(Vec<Value>),
    Object(Map<String, Value>),
}

// Represents a JSON null value. let v = json!(null);

// Represents a JSON boolean. let v = json!(true);

// Represents a JSON number, whether integer or floating point. let v = json!(12.5);

// Represents a JSON string. let v = json!("a string");

// Represents a JSON array. let v = json!(["an", "array"]);

// Represents a JSON object. By default the map is backed by a BTreeMap. Enable the preserve_order feature of serde_json to use IndexMap instead, which preserves entries in the order they are inserted into the map. In particular, this allows JSON data to be deserialized into a Value and serialized to a string while retaining the order of map keys in the input. let v = json!({ "an": "object" });
```
